label: Modal ontological argument on the case profile with an explicit de dicto to de re bridge
summary: Lane F (#2103). Instantiated the stipulated G of NecessaryIfExistent (#437) on the case: G v says some x that is GOD_4 under the case signature's primitive IsGod is concrete under the case profile and exists at v under its Ontic. Concreteness is not derived from necessity; it is taken from the possibility premise (#2106). Box G is definitionally DeDicto of that presence (#435), so its witnesses may vary across worlds. The passage to de re NecessaryAt is the explicit open premise GodPresencePersistsAt: every concrete GOD_4 at w exists at every accessible world at which some concrete GOD_4 exists. It asserts no existence and no uniqueness. Result 0149a95b derives NecessaryConcreteAt (b19ffd92) directly, with no transcription hop, from five premises. Two are root-path frame premises at the selected world only: EuclideanAt (1b1462e6) and ActualReflexive (2b20b5af). The other three are new and open: the boxed conditional, possibility and persistence. The sense passage NECESSARY_11 (Box over the frame) to NECESSARY_2 (NecessaryAt) is declared through the persistence premise, matching the proof. No excluded middle is used. Neither Scott's nor Gödel's essence-based NecessaryExistence and no Gödel GodLike occurs, so no Gödel-Scott God concept is identified with GOD_4; GOD_4 enters only as the predicate of G, with no naming premise. Review repair (#2160): the first version used GodPresenceRigidAt (e3c64b61) as the bridge. Given reflexivity at w, rigidity also entails at most one concrete GOD_4 at w and, if one exists there, cross-world uniqueness, which the conclusion does not use. Rigidity is now a sibling, registered as strengthening persistence. The backing instantiation is persists_of_rigid, and the strictness model is fixedPlusVisitor, where persistence holds and rigidity fails. Rigidity is weaker than pairwise identity across accessible worlds only given reflexivity at w; otherwise the two are incomparable. Controls result bc8eea6a: omitting each new premise (keeping the other four) falsifies the conclusion; a nonvacuity model satisfies all five premises; the strictness model also shows that the conclusion entails neither bridge sibling. The warrant question for the bridge is no longer classical uniqueness of God but GOD_4's cross-world stability: where a concrete GOD_4 exists at an accessible world, the one at w is among them. Candidate rivals bearing on it, recorded with their mechanisms but not yet assessed: (i) counterpart theory. Its mechanism is that world-bound individuals deny literal trans-world identity, so the role-filler at an accessible world is a counterpart and persistence in this rigid-candidate sense fails; compare the counterpart necessity controls in TruthCore.Modal.CounterpartNecessityControls. (ii) A replaceable divine role, whose mechanism is that different individuals fill the GOD_4 role at different worlds; the swapped model is its formal shape. Neither has a positive account recorded against this premise yet, so no substantive objection is on file. Rejected: (a) targeting the world-free GodExists, which the possibility premise alone already gives, so the modal steps would be idle; (b) a separate GOD_4 de re intermediate reached only through an assembly projection. Remaining: positive warrant for the three new premises, and the exact weaker frame condition SuccessorConnected (0523281a) in place of EuclideanAt.
